health.title: PC check-up
health.sub: Full check: disks, crashes, drivers, security, temperatures, memory and network.
opt.title: Optimize
opt.sub: Pick what you use the PC for most and I will enable the right settings. You can also switch single items on and off.
opt.legend: Green = safe. Yellow = read the note. Every change can be undone from the Restore section.

apply.norp: Note: Windows did not create the restore point (System Protection off or one already made today). Changes can still be undone from the Restore section.
apply.reboot: Some changes only take effect after a restart.
wiz.title: One-click optimization
wiz.sub: What do you use this PC for most? I will pick only safe changes that suit your hardware.
wiz.pick: Choose one of the options above.
wiz.summary: I will enable {0} optimizations and disable {1} useless services.
wiz.nothing: For this use your PC is already optimized!

proc.title: Processes & services
proc.sub: Fewer background programs = more free RAM and CPU for games and renders. I always tell you what would stop working.
proc.level.q: How much do you want to reduce?
proc.level.1.d: Only 100% safe things. No side effects.
proc.level.2.d: More, but anything you use (printer, Bluetooth...) is skipped automatically.
proc.level.3.d: The bare minimum. Read the yellow notes before applying.
proc.startup.help: Switches apply instantly. Off = the program no longer starts by itself when you turn on the PC (you can still open it manually).

boost.title: Boosting
net.title: Network & Ping
net.sub: Measure and improve ping, stability and connection for online gaming.
net.k.timer.h: Lower = Windows reacts sooner (0.5 ms is the minimum)
net.load.title: Ping under load
net.load.sub: The most important test for gaming: how much your ping rises when the line is busy (e.g. someone at home downloads or watches Netflix).
net.load.phase.load: Filling the line and measuring ping...
net.load.v.ok: Great: with the line full your ping only rises by {0} ms. Your connection holds up even when others download.
net.load.v.warn: Your ping rises by {0} ms when the line is full: if someone downloads at home you will lag. Enable QoS/SQM on your router or limit downloads while playing.
net.load.v.crit: Your ping rises by {0} ms under load (bufferbloat): the classic cause of "mysterious" lag. Enable QoS/SQM on your router; if it has none, consider one that does.
net.ping.title: Ping & stability test
net.ping.sub: 40 measurements to your router and major Internet servers. Jitter is how much the ping jumps around: lower means smoother games.
net.dns.title: Fastest DNS
net.dns.sub: DNS turns site names into addresses. A fast one speeds up loading, websites and connecting to servers.
net.dns.norevert: You have not changed DNS with Piki Optimizer.
net.reset.q: Resets all Windows network settings to default. Useful if the Internet acts strangely. Needs a restart and you will have to re-enter your Wi-Fi password.
net.reset.done: Network reset. Restart the PC to finish.
ae.sub: Smooth previews, faster renders and no crashes.
ae.render.title: Render Mode
ae.render.sub: Before a long render: maximum performance, the PC will not sleep, widgets and animated wallpapers are closed and After Effects and Media Encoder get high priority.
ae.render.status: On. Closed: {0}. Remember to turn it off after rendering.
ae.render.offstatus: Render Mode off: everything is back as before.
ae.settings.sub: Calculated for your hardware. The grey path tells you where to find them inside After Effects.
ae.folders: Create cache folders on the best drive
ae.close.first: Close After Effects, Premiere and Media Encoder before cleaning the cache.
ae.noinstall: After Effects is not installed: specific optimizations will appear as soon as you install it.
clean.title: Cleanup
clean.sub: Free up space by deleting only useless files. Documents, photos, games and passwords are never touched.
restore.title: Restore
restore.sub: Every Piki Optimizer change is saved here and can be undone with one click, even months later.
restore.point.sub: A "snapshot" of the system to go back to if something goes wrong.
restore.point.fail: Windows could not create the restore point (System Protection off?).
restore.all.sub: Puts every setting Piki Optimizer changed back the way it was.
restore.all.q: Do you really want to put everything back as it was before Piki Optimizer?
set.title: Settings
set.lang.sub: The app restarts to change language.
set.expert.sub: Also show advanced optimizations and technical details (registry keys, service names).
set.update.sub: Checks for a new version at startup. Only downloads the files that changed, in seconds.
set.about.text:
Piki Optimizer detects your PC's components and applies only documented, reversible optimizations. Nothing changes without you seeing it first. Use at your own risk: for any problem there is always the Undo button and the restore point.

Privacy: Piki Optimizer collects and sends no personal data. Everything stays on your PC; the only connections are the update check and the network tests you start.

set.tray.sub: When you close the window, Piki Optimizer stays in the notification area (next to the clock) with CPU and RAM always at hand.

fix.restart.text: Save your open work: the PC restarts right away.
fix.bios.text:
The PC restarts straight into the BIOS (UEFI).

• EXPO/XMP: look for "EXPO" or "XMP" (on MSI: F7 > OC > A-XMP/EXPO) and enable Profile 1.
• Secure Boot: Settings > Security > Secure Boot > Enabled.
• Hardware errors (WHEA): set overclocking back to "Auto" or press F6 for defaults.

Save with F10. Save your work before continuing.
update.offline: Updates are not available right now: check your connection and try again later.
net.boost.title: Optimize connection
net.boost.sub: One click: network card without power saving, maximum buffers, packets sent immediately, no Windows limit while gaming, no hidden uploads and the fastest DNS for you.
net.boost.next: Now run the ping test to see the result. If the "under load" test scores C or worse, the bottleneck is the router (enable QoS/SQM).
remote.title: Remote help
remote.sub: Control another PC remotely or let someone help you, like AnyDesk. Uses Microsoft Quick Assist: free, encrypted and already part of Windows.
remote.get.d: Someone you trust will see and control this PC. They give you a 6-character code: enter it, then accept. You can end the connection at any time.
remote.give.d: See and control a friend's PC. Sign in with a Microsoft account, choose "Help someone" and give the code to the other person.
remote.warn.title: Beware of scams
remote.warn: Microsoft, your bank or fake "technicians" will never call you to ask for a remote access code. Only give the code to people you really know.
remote.opened: Quick Assist is open: follow the instructions in its window.
remote.install: Quick Assist is not installed: Microsoft Store has opened, press "Get" and try again.
